name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
executive_summary: Combine a parametric generator with a non-parametric retrieval index: retrieve relevant documents for the query, then condition generation on both the query and the retrieved text.
description: Rather than relying solely on knowledge implicitly stored in model weights, a retriever (originally dense passage retrieval over a Wikipedia index) fetches the top-k relevant documents for the input, which are concatenated with the query and passed to the generator. The foundational paper for the entire retrieval-augmented family of techniques, and the implicit threat model behind any 'insufficient retrieval / say you don't know' guardrail.
when_to_use: Knowledge-intensive tasks where the required facts are unlikely to be reliably present in the model's parametric knowledge, or where up-to-date/external/proprietary information is needed.
when_not_to_use: No retrieval index/corpus is available, or the task is purely reasoning-based with no external-fact dependency.
known_pitfalls: If retrieval returns nothing relevant, the generator can still confabulate rather than acknowledging insufficient evidence — this is exactly the failure mode a 'RAG shield' / insufficient-retrieval guardrail needs to catch.

primary_source.authors: Lewis, Perez, Piktus, Petroni, Karpukhin, Goyal, Küttler, Lewis, Yih, Rocktäschel, Riedel, Kiela
primary_source.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template depends on an external system (retrieval index, tool, solver, or interpreter) whose own behavior is outside the prompt's control; bit-for-bit reproducibility requires that system's state to also be fixed.
